pr_title: Track source for arrays of objects
pr_body:
This PR uses option `store_array_source` for objects to track the source of (sub)object arrays in synthetic mode. This allows preserving the original source, as synthetic mode merges, deduplicates and sorts array entries by default. The downside is that the whole object array (including children objects and fields) gets stored twice, while there's additional overhead while synthesizing source at query time.

This functionality will be experimental initially, to get some experience before documenting and opening up its use.

Fixes #90708
pr_comments: Hi @kkrik-es, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> Should we add documentation for new parameter?

I was thinking of keeping it experimental initially, until Observability provides feedback on its use. @felixbarny fyi.
The `store_array_source` flag looks good to me, I've pinged the team to test it and provide feedback.

issue_context.title: Synthetic _source: preserve source for specific fields (object arrays)
comments: Generally speaking, allowing to configure synthetic _source per field instead of per index in certain situations would be useful in multiple scenarios even beyond APM. We need to examine alternatives for how to develop it (design details), and prioritize it in comparison to other roadmap items.

For fields that are only stored in the `_source` (either via `store=false`, `index=false`, `doc_values=false`, or via `dynamic=false`), such as APM stack traces, maybe we could even automatically preserve them by putting their source in a hidden stored field.
This feature sound very interesting to help adoption of the synthetic _source, is there any plan to implement it? Thank you!
Hello @giladgal, will you implement this feature? If yes I would like to work on it.

@axw I believe with the `store_array_source` setting implemented in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/108417 and objects with `enabled: false` being preserved in synthetic source, too (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/108051), we could enable synthetic source in the APM plugin component templates. What would be a good way to test that?
@felixbarny nice. A reasonably straightforward option would be to create a serverless project, and create a `traces@custom` component template that enables synthetic source.

review_comments: Can this method be moved to `XContentDataHelperTests`? This is the only place where it is used.
@lkts will be using it in his PR.
I see, then let's leave it here.

Maybe also add unit tests to `DocumentParserTests` that test with store array source? Including some tests with multi levels of object array fields and store array source param being enabled on different levels.
I added tests in `IgnoredSourceFieldMapperTests`, along with the rest of the tests for extended synthetic source. Any suggestions for scenarios to cover?
I missed that the tests in `IgnoredSourceFieldMapperTests` also invoke this method. The tests `IgnoredSourceFieldMapperTests` look good to me.
Maybe these methods instead of returning a tuple should return a record? I think `getParserContext()` or `getBuilder()` reads easier than `v1()` and `v2()`?
Since we just need to wrap a couple of objects and there are no methods, I'd think a tuple is a good match here.
I did change the call sites to skip using `var`, it's should be more readable now.

This is a new usage of the switchParser() method. However it is currently deprecated. I think if we like to use then we should un-deprecate this method. I think this new usage is a valid use case. cc: @javanna

Looking at the concerns we had with switchParser, i think your assessment is right. Also, its javadocs says

>  we are actively deprecating and removing the ability to pass complex objects to multifields, so try and avoid using this method

Given that this was committed 4 years ago, the "actively" part no longer holds true. I reviewed the current usages of switchParser and they seem ok to me. I have a slight concern that we are now using the method in a general utility method, that may spread its usage instead of limiting it to the only places where it's strictly needed. I am not sure what to do about that though, and I am ok with the current plan. Thanks for raising this.
